links_touching_record.rationale: Implementation element FB2-SW-IMP-000001 is the code location in which FB2-SW-DSN-000001's acquisition, PEC-validation and publication responsibilities are carried: the pinned source's LTC_Trigger sequencer, its LTC_StartVoltageMeasurement command selection, its LTC_CheckPec per-LTC integrity gate and its LTC_SaveRxToVoltageBuffer reassembly into the published database block. The link runs from the implementation to the design because that is the direction master prompt section 13 declares for implements (implementation element -> design/requirement).

FB2-SW-IMP-000001 realises FB2-SW-SWR-000001 at the requirement level: the acquisition the statement calls for is triggered through AFE_StartMeasurement into the LTC sequencer, the PEC validation it calls for is LTC_CheckPec's per-LTC comparison, and the publication it calls for is the DATA_WRITE_DATA path. The requirement's own quantified figures - 20 Hz, 5 ms, 100% - are not established by this link, and the implementation record marks them as modelled rather than read from source.

behaviours.description: Starts a measurement cycle by submitting an LTC_STATE_INIT_REQUEST to the per-driver state request setter, which is what the task layer calls each cycle.
Selects and transmits one of the ltc_cmdADCV_* commands for a full-cell or two-cell ADC measurement, and refuses to transmit for an unsupported mode/channel combination.
Recomputes the 15-bit PEC for each LTC in the daisy chain and records the comparison result per LTC, so a corrupted frame is marked rather than consumed.
Reassembles the cell voltages from the received byte pairs of each register group and writes them into the database block, skipping channels the configuration marks unused.
Publishes the parsed voltage block to the database; the database write path stamps the block header with the current tick so every published block carries an age.
The CRC-15 polynomial used for the LTC packet error code, shared by every LTC-family backend.
Configures the paired SPI transmit and receive DMA channels for the frame, elevating privilege for the register write, and lets the completion interrupt finish the transfer.
Clears the driver's transmit-in-progress flag when the DMA receive-complete interrupt reports that the transfer finished.

concurrency_and_isr_context.shared_state: ltc_state, the per-driver LTC_STATE_s, written by the task and read by the same task; the sequencer guards re-entrance with LTC_CheckReEntrance (ltc_6813-1.c:748-761). The transmit_in_progress flag it also holds is written from the DMA driver's receive-complete interrupt by AFE_DmaCallback and cleared by the task, which is the one genuinely cross-context interaction in this element.

limitations: The content_hash recorded here is the sha256 of the file AT THE PINNED COMMIT. For this file it is also the sha256 of the working-tree copy, so the working tree and the pin agree; for files where they differ this distinction matters and is stated in the relevant record.
Existence was verified. Behaviour was verified by reading the code. Nothing here was executed, and no measurement of this module's timing, coverage or throughput exists in this corpus.

The design record FB2-SW-DSN-000001 asserts four implementation symbols that do not exist anywhere in the repository. Those assertions were not carried into this record and are not corrected here, because the design record is a separate artefact; the disagreement is stated in implements.partial_coverage and in this record's provenance_note.
evidence_status.method: For each code_location: the file was read at the pinned commit with 'git show 308028fb:path'; the file's sha256 was computed from that pinned blob and is the value recorded in content_hash; the named symbol was confirmed to occur inside the recorded line_range of that pinned content, and the line range was confirmed to lie within the pinned file's length. Line ranges were cross-read against 'graft skeleton' output for the same files, which reports definition line spans independently of this authoring pass. The DMA path was additionally confirmed by reading SPI_TransmitReceiveDataDma in spi.c, AFE_DmaCallback in ltc_afe_dma.c, and the DMA driver's receive-complete interrupt case in dma.c at the pinned commit.

guard.statement: This record says where the code for FB2-SW-DSN-000001's acquisition path is and what that code does. It is not evidence that FB2-SW-SWR-000001 is met: the quantified acceptance criteria of that requirement (20 Hz acquisition, 5 ms publication latency, 100% PEC coverage) are not established by any location listed here, and the two measures that address them carry their own outcome, which in the as_is profile is a host-run record with its own limitations. It confers no production authority and no product verification credit, and no human has approved it.

partial_coverage: The design's implementation_mapping asserts four symbols - LTC_AFE_TriggerMeasurement, LTC_AFE_DMA_RxCallback, LTC_PEC_Calculate and LTC_6813_ReadVoltages - and two paths, src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe.c and src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c. None of the four symbols occurs anywhere in the repository. Of the two paths, ltc_afe_dma.c does exist and is where the DMA completion callback AFE_DmaCallback lives; ltc_afe.c does not exist - the module is at src/app/driver/afe/ltc/api/ltc_afe.c. The design's DMA mechanism is therefore substantively realised and its symbol names and one of its two paths are wrong; this record names the symbols and paths that exist and does not adopt the design's spelling.

The design's 'DMA buffer size: 256 bytes per slave' constraint has no counterpart this record can point at. The realised transfer sizes its DMA channel from the frame length passed to SPI_TransmitReceiveDataDma rather than from a fixed per-slave buffer of that size, and no 256-byte per-slave buffer was found in the AFE code. The constraint is recorded as unevidenced rather than claimed as met.

The design's 'database publishing' happens through the DATA_WRITE_DATA macro (ltc_6813-1.c:653), which timestamps the block header in database.c:160-194 (DATA_CopyData sets previousTimestamp and timestamp from OS_GetTickCount). The design says nothing about timestamping; the code carries a per-block age that the design does not describe.

The design's balancing behaviour is only partially realised in this file: LTC_BalanceControl (ltc_6813-1.c:3453-3583) and LTC_SaveBalancingFeedback (710-720) exist in the same translation unit, but this record scopes itself to the voltage acquisition path and does not claim the balancing behaviour as realised.

The design's temperature read (state READ_TEMPERATURES) is realised by the same sequencer through LTC_StartGpioMeasurement (3727-3781) rather than by a separate temperature command sequence, which is a structural difference from the design's two-state split.

The design's 'Task period: 100 ms' and 'Stack usage: < 2 KB' constraints are not established by anything in this record. No task period or stack figure for this module is measured or recorded anywhere in this corpus.
implements.relationship: This translation unit is where FB2-SW-DSN-000001's acquisition, PEC-validation and publication responsibilities are actually carried. The mechanism, read from the pinned source: AFE_StartMeasurement (ltc_afe.c:142-150) submits an LTC_STATE_INIT_REQUEST to LTC_SetStateRequest, which is the entry into LTC_Trigger's step sequencer; LTC_StartVoltageMeasurement (ltc_6813-1.c:3678-3711) sends one of the ltc_cmdADCV_* commands, selecting between fast/normal/filtered ADC modes and between all-channel and two-cell channel selection, and returns STD_NOT_OK for any other combination rather than transmitting; LTC_CheckPec (3838-3878) recomputes a 15-bit PEC per LTC from the six received bytes with LTC_CalculatePec15 (ltc_pec.c:75-115) and compares it byte-for-byte against the two received PEC bytes, writing PEC_valid[stringNumber][i] into the error table and returning STD_NOT_OK on the first mismatch unless LTC_DISCARD_PEC is set; LTC_SaveRxToVoltageBuffer (3064-3150) reassembles three voltages per register group from the little-endian byte pairs at offset 4 + 2*c + 8*m and writes the result into ltc_state->ltcData.cellVoltage, after which DATA_WRITE_DATA publishes the block. The DMA transfer the design selects is not in this file but is real and is carried by the SPI driver (SPI_TransmitReceiveDataDma, src/app/driver/spi/spi.c:403-511) with completion signalled through AFE_DmaCallback (src/app/driver/afe/ltc/common/ltc_afe_dma.c:88-93), which the DMA driver calls from its receive-complete interrupt when FOXBMS_AFE_DRIVER_LTC is 1 (src/app/driver/dma/dma.c:393-400). So the design's INIT -> READ_VOLTAGES -> VALIDATE -> PUBLISH sequence is realised as a table-driven sequencer plus a per-LTC PEC gate plus a DMA-backed SPI transfer plus a block write, not as the seven-state machine the design record draws.

realises_requirements.how_realised: Acquisition is started through AFE_StartMeasurement -> LTC_SetStateRequest -> LTC_Trigger; integrity is gated by LTC_CheckPec, which invalidates the per-LTC PEC_valid flag on a mismatch and only then permits the parsed values to reach the database block; publication is DATA_WRITE_DATA(ltc_state->ltcData.cellVoltage) at ltc_6813-1.c:653, whose database handler stamps a timestamp. That is the three-part mechanism the requirement's statement describes (trigger acquisition, validate PEC, publish).

required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.

target.primary_key_rule: ID-RULE-004-A1: an artefact identifier is unique within its profile; two records of different profiles may carry the same identifier string.
